shortName: Wright State University Boonshoft School of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
Additional information regarding prerequisite courses can be found here: https://medicine.wright.edu/admissions/prerequisites-and-application

Any Advanced Placement (AP) or other courses must appear on your university's official academic transcript to meet prerequisite requirements. 

Community college credit is accepted if it includes a lab component and is comparable in content to a four-year college. 

Only Math and English requirements can be taken as online classes. Online science prerequisites are not accepted unless offered online as a result of the Novel Coronavirus Pandemic. Please contact our office at som-admissions@wright.edu upon completing your secondary application to verify these online prerequisite courses.

There is no requirement to take these courses within a particular time frame, but most applicants find that courses completed more than 10 years ago will not be current enough to adequately prepare them for the MCAT.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Office of Student Affairs and Admissions exists to serve and support Boonshoft School of Medicine students from the time they apply for admission until the time they graduate from medical school and enter residency training. The office is located on the first floor of White Hall, adjacent to the Atrium. A pre-matriculation program, mentoring, big brother/big sister program, tutoring, USMLE preparation, and assistance in critical thinking and learning are available. Student interest groups include SNMA, LMSA, Pride, and Women in Surgery. For additional information, please navigate to https://medicine.wright.edu/student-life
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence may be granted for academic, personal, or health reasons. In most cases, leaves do not exceed one year. Academic leave is available to students in good academic standing who wish to pursue research or related scholarly activity. Medical leave is available to students who seek treatment for health-related conditions that interfere with one's abilities to participate in educational programs. Personal leave is available to enable students to take time off, in special circumstances, for reasons unrelated to health or academics.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The School supports more than 60 student organizations, including 17 student interest groups, 18 specialty interest groups, and 10 national organizations with Boonshoft chapters. Students across all four years are heavily involved in one or several organizations, often also participating in university-wide intramural sports. Further information about the wide range of student interest groups, as well as contact information, can be found on the BSOM student life web page.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Foundations phase of the curriculum occurs on the main Wright State campus in an affordable suburban area of Dayton. The medical school building has ample and comfortable study space, classrooms designed for engaged learning, student lounge, clinical skills center, and open meeting space.  A full-service student union (cafeteria, bank, gym with a pool, squash and racquetball courts, climbing wall, bookstore) is a two-minute walk.  Dayton has extensive bike-paths and parks, a range of entertainment, and considerable cultural depth, including a symphony, opera, dance, ballet, art and science museums, minor league baseball team, and very accessible libraries.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Housing is available at reasonable costs on campus, adjacent to campus and throughout the Dayton area.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Boonshoft School of Medicine aims to provide a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment for LGBTQA individuals. The medical student organization Boonshoft Pride promotes awareness and establishes an identifiable network of allies. Furthermore, the organization aims to extend medical education to encompass health-related LGBT issues through talks, panels, and community outreach. For additional information, please navigate to https://medicine.wright.edu/student-life/student-organizations/boonshoft-pride
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Disability Services (ODS) recognizes disability as an aspect of diversity that is integral to society and to our campus community. Accessibility is an essential feature of the Wright State campus, and we strive to create an inclusive community for our students, faculty, staff, and guests. For additional information, please navigate to https://www.wright.edu/disability-services
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Confidential psychiatric services, including counseling and medication management, are available to all medical students with professional courtesy. Individual psychotherapy, couples, and family counseling are also available. In addition, Project Wellness is an Integrative Health Interest Group dedicated to fostering whole-person wellness in health professionals and our patients. We are an interprofessional group of students dedicated to learning about the practice of integrative medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At Boonshoft School of Medicine, we pride ourselves on providing exceptional, engaging, and collaborative training to prepare today's most promising students to become tomorrow's most successful physicians. As a Wright State student, you will be part of a diverse group of carefully selected students who possess the potential to excel in academic and clinical work, and who demonstrate the maturity, motivation, selflessness and empathy that are the hallmarks of truly outstanding physicians.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: In addition to meeting with an academic advisor or study skills specialist, any student may request a paid upper-class tutor. Students may meet with their tutors up to 10 hours per week.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Classroom instruction uses engaging strategies with considerable peer and faculty interaction, with high expectation for out-of-class self-directed learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations in local community hospitals, clinics, and practices begin the third year. More information can be found at https://medicine.wright.edu/student-life/curriculum/wrightcurriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The WrightCurriculum, launched in 2017 for the class of 2021, was developed after extensive planning, content prioritization, and testing of teaching and learning strategies. It's founded on three key principles: fostering self-directed learners skilled in critical thinking and lifelong learning; employing evidence-based teaching methods linked to learning science; and continuously evolving through collaborative faculty-student feedback.

Structured in two phases—Foundations (19.5 months) and Doctoring (25.2 months) — the curriculum emphasizes integrated learning of normal and abnormal conditions through clinical application, moving away from traditional lecture-based models. It focuses on developmental learning goals, small class sizes, flipped classroom approaches, and significant faculty support, enhancing small group learning and individual progress tracking in knowledge, clinical skills, and professionalism.

Unique features include a lecture-free Foundations phase where classroom time is spent on problem-solving and applying pre-studied content, and the Doctoring phase that offers extensive clinical experiences and specialty clerkships, culminating in a final year tailored to student interests and robust residency preparation.

The curriculum also integrates extra-curricular activities, service learning, and over 60 student clubs and interest groups to develop well-rounded, humanistic physicians equipped for 21st-century healthcare. This supportive, collaborative learning environment not only prepares students for national licensing exams but also fosters personal and professional growth.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Our students gain vast knowledge and develop specialized skills to prepare them for success as confident, competent and compassionate physicians. We are proud to be nationally recognized for meeting our social mission as measured by the percentage of graduates who practice primary care and work in health professional shortage areas. Since its establishment, the School has employed an innovative community-based model, including affiliations with major teaching hospitals, to prepare students for the dynamic world of modern medicine. The curriculum emphasizes attention to the social determinants of health. Our reputation has steadily grown due to our award-winning faculty, pioneering dual-degree programs, integrated team-based learning, and graduates who consistently excel in top residency and fellowship programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Wright State University is home to outstanding research facilities, faculty at the forefront of their fields, and ample funding to support groundbreaking investigations in basic and clinical science. In addition, we are affiliated with a wide range of universities, government, and industry partners that vastly expand the scope and nature of our research. In every department, work underway at Wright State University is helping to shape the future of medicine.  Research (biomedical, clinical, public health) and other opportunities for scholarship support the curricular requirement for completing a scholarly project at WSU-BSOM. Two full-time masters-level and Ph.D. staff are devoted to assisting students with the design of projects, linkages to faculty, and guidance for writing and presenting.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The WrightCurriculum is structured in two phases—Foundations (73 weeks) and Doctoring (102 weeks)
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community engagement is an integral part of the curriculum. In addition, nearly all student organizations incorporate service into their mission.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Scholarship in Medicine ensures that students engage in instruction in the scientific method and collect and/or use data to test and verify hypotheses and address questions about biomedical phenomena.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The School has over 30 affiliated healthcare institutions. Most experiences occur in a children's hospital, two rural hospitals, two federal hospitals, and four large acute care hospitals.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail during Foundations Phase, Honors/Pass/Fail during Doctoring Phase core clerkships and Pass/Fail during Doctoring Phase non-core clerkships.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Boonshoft School of Medicine is a community-based medical school established in 1974. Clinical facilities include eight major teaching hospitals with over 2,700 patient beds. A faculty of over 1,200 provides students with opportunities for individualized attention.  The School emphasizes community engagement, research, generalist training, patient focused care, cultural competence and diversity, health promotion, disease prevention, and the provision of care to underserved populations.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We transform lives through our commitment to outstanding education, innovative research, community partnerships, and exemplary clinical care. We amplify diversity and belonging as we advance health in Ohio’s communities and beyond.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
To fulfill our letters of recommendation requirement, applicants must submit at least three (3) and no more than five (5) letters of recommendation through the AMCAS Letter Service.  All letters must:
- Be submitted through the AMCAS Letter Service (not directly to the medical school)
- Be on official letterhead and include the author's signature
- Be received by August 31st for Early Decision applicants, and December 1st for Regular Decision applicants
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Letters of Recommendation may come from any individuals an applicant chooses, but we strongly encourage applicants to select letter writers who know them well and can meaningfully speak to their abilities to meet the academic rigor of medical school and to their character as an applicant.

While not required, a committee letter packet from your undergraduate premedical advising office will fully meet our requirement alone, as it includes multiple authors.  

Whether submitting individual letters or a committee letter packet, all letters must:
- Be submitted through the AMCAS Letter Service (not directly to the medical school)
- Be on official letterhead and include the author's signature
- Be received by August 31st for Early Decision applicants, and December 1st for Regular Decision applicants
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations for interviews are emailed beginning in August with interviews starting in late August.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two, one-on-one virtual interviews, each lasting 45-60 minutes.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The Medical College Admissions Test (MCAT) and three years (90 semester hours or 135 quarter hours) of preparation in an approved college or university in the United States or Canada are required for admission to Boonshoft School of Medicine. Applicants are expected to present the equivalent of the usual premedical preparation, including the following:

Two semesters or three quarters of college biology with labs; college general chemistry with labs; college organic chemistry with labs; college physics with labs; college English and college mathematics ( statistics may be substituted for one mathematics course); One Semester or two quarters of biochemistry.

There is no requirement to take these courses within a particular time frame, but most applicants find that courses completed more than 10 years ago are not current enough to adequately prepare them for the MCAT.

All prerequisite coursework must be completed and verified by official transcript prior to the start of the program.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The School seeks a student body of diverse social, ethnic, and educational backgrounds. Applicants are admitted solely on the basis of individual qualifications without regard to race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status, national origin, age, or ancestry. Dedication to human concerns, compassion, intellectual capacity, and maturity are of greater importance than specific areas of preprofessional preparation. The School also values evidence of motivation, altruism, leadership, and communication skills. Also considered are the applicant's academic record, MCAT performance, letters of recommendation, history of military and community service, and the results of a personal interview (by invitation). Both Ohio residents and non-residents are encouraged to apply.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Premedical shadowing is recommended to provide evidence that an applicant is familiar with the day-to-day requirements of a professional career in the medical field and is able to express why he/she feels passionate that it is the ideal profession for them. Other clinically and medically-related experiences will fulfill this purpose as well. The committee is looking for evidence that the applicant has sufficiently explored their career choice.
